explanation.en: Present **don't** backshifts to past **didn't** in reported speech.
explanation.vi: Hiện tại **don't** lùi thành quá khứ **didn't** trong câu tường thuật.
explanation.id: Present **don't** bergeser ke past **didn't** dalam kalimat tidak langsung.
explanation.hi: "said" past में → "went" (past) backshift होकर "had gone" (past perfect) बनेगा।

title.en: Passive voice — don't drop **be**
title.vi: Câu bị động — đừng bỏ **be**

hook.en: "The letter written yesterday." Almost every Indonesian learner writes this — because "surat itu ditulis kemarin" is already a complete sentence in Indonesian. But English needs one more word.
hook.vi: "The letter written yesterday." Hầu như bạn học Indonesia nào cũng viết vậy — vì "surat itu ditulis kemarin" đã là câu hoàn chỉnh trong tiếng Indonesia. Nhưng tiếng Anh cần thêm một từ nữa.
hook.ja: 「The letter written yesterday.」— 日本語の「手紙は昨日書かれた」の感覚で書いてしまいがちです。しかし英語の受動態には、必ず **be動詞** が必要です。
hook.id: "The letter written yesterday." Hampir semua pelajar Indonesia menulis seperti ini — karena "surat itu ditulis kemarin" sudah kalimat lengkap dalam bahasa Indonesia. Tapi bahasa Inggris butuh satu kata lagi.

why.en: Indonesian forms the passive with the **di-** prefix (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). One word is enough. English needs two pieces: a form of **be** + the past participle (V3). Without **be**, the sentence sounds broken to a native ear.
why.vi: Tiếng Indonesia tạo bị động bằng tiền tố **di-** (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). Một từ là đủ. Tiếng Anh cần hai phần: dạng **be** + quá khứ phân từ (V3). Thiếu **be**, câu nghe như gãy với tai người bản xứ.
why.ja: 日本語の受身（「〜れる」「〜られる」）は動詞の語尾変化で表します。英語の受動態は **be動詞 + 過去分詞** の2語で作り、**be動詞** を省略することは絶対にできません。
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia membentuk pasif dengan awalan **di-** (ditulis, dimakan, dibangun). Satu kata sudah cukup. Bahasa Inggris perlu dua bagian: bentuk **be** + past participle (V3). Tanpa **be**, kalimatnya terdengar patah bagi penutur asli.

pattern.en: English passive = **be + past participle (V3)**. Present: **is/are + written**. Past: **was/were + written**. Present perfect: **has/have been + written**. Future: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**
pattern.vi: Bị động tiếng Anh = **be + quá khứ phân từ (V3)**. Hiện tại: **is/are + written**. Quá khứ: **was/were + written**. Hiện tại hoàn thành: **has/have been + written**. Tương lai: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**
pattern.ja: 英語の受動態 = **be + 過去分詞（V3）**。現在：**is/are + written**。過去：**was/were + written**。現在完了：**has/have been + written**。未来：**will be + written**。**The letter was written yesterday.**（手紙は昨日書かれた）**The food is cooked every morning.**（料理は毎朝作られる）**The bridge will be built next year.**（橋は来年建設される）
pattern.id: Pasif bahasa Inggris = **be + past participle (V3)**. Present: **is/are + written**. Past: **was/were + written**. Present perfect: **has/have been + written**. Future: **will be + written**. **The letter was written yesterday.** **The food is cooked every morning.** **The bridge will be built next year.**

practice.en: Say each aloud and feel the **be** sitting in the middle: "The letter was written yesterday." (NOT "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận **be** nằm giữa câu: "The letter was written yesterday." (KHÔNG phải "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."
practice.ja: 声に出して、**be動詞** が文の中心にある感覚をつかみましょう：「The letter was written yesterday.」（「The letter written yesterday.」ではない）「The food is prepared fresh daily.」「English is spoken here.」「The work was finished on time.」「A new mall will be built here.」
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan rasakan **be** duduk di tengahnya: "The letter was written yesterday." (BUKAN "The letter written yesterday.") "The food is prepared fresh daily." "English is spoken here." "The work was finished on time." "A new mall will be built here."

takeaway.en: Passive = **be + V3**. Always. The **be** is never optional.
takeaway.vi: Bị động = **be + V3**. Luôn luôn. Không bao giờ được bỏ **be**.
takeaway.ja: 受動態 = **be + 過去分詞**。常に。**be動詞** は絶対に省略不可。
takeaway.id: Pasif = **be + V3**. Selalu. **be** tidak pernah opsional.

question.en: Which sentence is correct?
question.vi: Câu nào đúng?
question.id: Kalimat mana yang benar?

question.en: Fill in the blank: English ___ spoken in many countries.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: English ___ spoken in many countries.
question.id: Isi bagian kosong: English ___ spoken in many countries.

explanation.vi: **English** = số ít → **is + spoken** (bị động hiện tại).
explanation.ja: **English** = 単数 → **is + spoken**（現在の受動態）。
explanation.id: **English** = tunggal → **is + spoken** (pasif present).

question.en: Fill in the blank (past): The windows ___ broken during the storm.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống (quá khứ): The windows ___ broken during the storm.
question.id: Isi bagian kosong (lampau): The windows ___ broken during the storm.

explanation.en: **windows** = plural + past → **were + broken**.
explanation.vi: **windows** = số nhiều + quá khứ → **were + broken**.
explanation.ja: **windows** = 複数 + 過去 → **were + broken**。

question.en: Choose the correct passive form:

question.en: Fill in the blank (future): A new hospital ___ built next year.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống (tương lai): A new hospital ___ built next year.
question.id: Isi bagian kosong (masa depan): A new hospital ___ built next year.

explanation.en: Future passive = **will be + V3**. **will be built**, not **will built**.
explanation.vi: Bị động tương lai = **will be + V3**. **will be built**, không phải **will built**.
explanation.ja: 未来の受動態 = **will be + 過去分詞**。**will be built**、**will built** ではない。
explanation.id: Pasif masa depan = **will be + V3**. **will be built**, bukan **will built**.

title.en: Modal + **have** + V3 — talk about the past
title.vi: Modal + **have** + V3 — nói về quá khứ

hook.en: "I should did it." Every learner tries this — just put the modal and the past verb together, right? English has a different move: **should have done**. One extra word that changes everything.
hook.vi: "I should did it." Bạn nào cũng thử vậy — cứ ghép modal với động từ quá khứ là xong, đúng không? Tiếng Anh có một bước khác: **should have done**. Một từ thôi mà thay đổi tất cả.
hook.id: "I should did it." Setiap pelajar mencoba ini — tinggal gabungkan modal dan kata kerja lampau, kan? Bahasa Inggris punya langkah berbeda: **should have done**. Satu kata tambahan yang mengubah segalanya.

why.en: Vietnamese doesn't have a dedicated structure for past speculation or regret. **Lẽ ra** or **đáng lẽ** sits before the verb and the verb stays the same — **lẽ ra tôi nên học**. English forces **modal + have + V3** to push the speculation backward in time. The modal carries the meaning; **have + V3** carries the past.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình không có cấu trúc riêng cho suy đoán hay tiếc nuối quá khứ. **Lẽ ra** hoặc **đáng lẽ** đặt trước động từ và động từ giữ nguyên — **lẽ ra tôi nên học**. Tiếng Anh bắt buộc **modal + have + V3** để đẩy suy đoán về quá khứ. Modal mang nghĩa; **have + V3** mang thì quá khứ.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya struktur khusus untuk spekulasi atau penyesalan masa lampau. **Seharusnya** atau **semestinya** diletakkan sebelum kata kerja dan kata kerjanya tetap sama — **seharusnya saya belajar**. Bahasa Inggris memaksa **modal + have + V3** untuk mendorong spekulasi ke masa lampau. Modal membawa makna; **have + V3** membawa waktu lampau.

pattern.en: **modal + have + past participle (V3)**. For past regret: **should have + V3** (*I should have studied*). For past possibility: **could have + V3** (*She could have called*). For past deduction: **must have + V3** (*He must have forgotten*). For past hypothetical: **would have + V3** (*I would have helped*). The main verb NEVER goes directly after the modal in past form.
pattern.vi: **modal + have + quá khứ phân từ (V3)**. Tiếc nuối: **should have + V3** (*I should have studied*). Khả năng quá khứ: **could have + V3** (*She could have called*). Suy đoán quá khứ: **must have + V3** (*He must have forgotten*). Giả định quá khứ: **would have + V3** (*I would have helped*). Động từ chính KHÔNG BAO GIỜ đứng trực tiếp sau modal ở dạng quá khứ.
pattern.id: **modal + have + past participle (V3)**. Untuk penyesalan masa lalu: **should have + V3** (*I should have studied* — Seharusnya saya belajar). Untuk kemungkinan masa lalu: **could have + V3** (*She could have called* — Dia bisa saja menelepon). Untuk deduksi masa lalu: **must have + V3** (*He must have forgotten* — Dia pasti lupa). Untuk hipotesis masa lalu: **would have + V3** (*I would have helped* — Saya akan membantu). Kata kerja utama TIDAK PERNAH langsung setelah modal dalam bentuk lampau.

practice.en: Try these aloud and feel the **have** sitting between the modal and the V3 — it's never optional. "I should have called her yesterday." "You could have told me earlier." "He must have missed the bus." "She might have forgotten about it." "They would have come if they knew."
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng và cảm nhận **have** nằm giữa modal và V3 — không bao giờ được bỏ. "I should have called her yesterday." "You could have told me earlier." "He must have missed the bus." "She might have forgotten about it." "They would have come if they knew."
practice.id: Coba ucapkan dengan keras dan rasakan **have** duduk di antara modal dan V3 — tidak pernah opsional. "I should have called her yesterday." "You could have told me earlier." "He must have missed the bus." "She might have forgotten about it." "They would have come if they knew."

takeaway.en: Modal about the past → **modal + have + V3**. Never put a past-tense verb directly after a modal.
takeaway.vi: Modal nói về quá khứ → **modal + have + V3**. Không bao giờ đặt động từ quá khứ trực tiếp sau modal.
takeaway.id: Modal tentang masa lalu → **modal + have + V3**. Jangan pernah meletakkan kata kerja lampau langsung setelah modal.

question.en: I should ___ to her yesterday.
question.vi: I should ___ to her yesterday.

explanation.en: Past regret needs **should have + V3** — the **have** is mandatory.
explanation.vi: Tiếc nuối quá khứ cần **should have + V3** — **have** là bắt buộc.
explanation.id: Penyesalan masa lalu butuh **should have + V3** — **have** itu wajib.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: He must have missed the bus.
He must have miss the bus.
He must has missed the bus.
quiz.correctAnswer: He must have missed the bus.

explanation.en: **must have + V3** — the modal is followed by **have** (never **has**), then the past participle.
explanation.vi: **must have + V3** — modal đi với **have** (không bao giờ **has**), rồi đến quá khứ phân từ.
explanation.id: **must have + V3** — modal diikuti oleh **have** (bukan **has**), lalu past participle.

question.en: Fill in the blank: She ___ have told me earlier.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: She ___ have told me earlier.

explanation.en: Past possibility uses **could have + V3**. No **to** between the modal and **have**.
explanation.vi: Khả năng quá khứ dùng **could have + V3**. Không có **to** giữa modal và **have**.
explanation.id: Kemungkinan masa lalu menggunakan **could have + V3**. Tidak ada **to** di antara modal dan **have**.

question.en: Which sentence is correct?
question.vi: Câu nào đúng?

options: I should have done it yesterday.
I should have did it yesterday.
I should to do it yesterday.
quiz.correctAnswer: I should have done it yesterday.

explanation.en: **should have + V3**: **done** is the past participle of **do**. The modal-perfect structure never uses the simple past form.
explanation.vi: **should have + V3**: **done** là quá khứ phân từ của **do**. Cấu trúc modal-perfect không bao giờ dùng dạng quá khứ đơn.
explanation.id: **should have + V3**: **done** adalah past participle dari **do**. Struktur modal-perfect tidak pernah menggunakan bentuk simple past.

question.en: They ___ have come if they had known about the party.
question.vi: They ___ have come if they had known about the party.

explanation.en: Past hypothetical third conditional: **would have + V3** in the main clause.
explanation.vi: Giả định quá khứ câu điều kiện loại 3: **would have + V3** ở mệnh đề chính.
explanation.id: Hipotesis masa lalu conditional type 3: **would have + V3** di klausa utama.

title.en: **If I were** — the unreal past form
title.vi: **If I were** — dạng giả định không có thật

hook.en: "If I was you, I would take the job." Sounds close — but English has a special form for unreal situations: **If I were you**. It's one of the last grammar moves advanced learners master, and it signals C1 control.
hook.vi: "If I was you, I would take the job." Nghe gần đúng — nhưng tiếng Anh có một dạng đặc biệt cho tình huống không có thật: **If I were you**. Đây là một trong những điểm ngữ pháp cuối cùng mà người học nâng cao mới làm chủ được, và nó thể hiện trình độ C1.
hook.id: "If I was you, I would take the job." Kedengarannya hampir benar — tapi bahasa Inggris punya bentuk khusus untuk situasi yang tidak nyata: **If I were you**. Ini adalah salah satu poin tata bahasa terakhir yang dikuasai pelajar tingkat lanjut, dan menandakan kemampuan C1.

why.en: Vietnamese doesn't mark a difference between real and unreal conditions in the verb form. **Nếu tôi là bạn** uses the same **là** as any other sentence. English uses **were** (not **was**) after **if** or **wish** when the situation is imagined, hypothetical, or contrary to fact — for EVERY subject, even **I**, **he**, and **she**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình không đánh dấu sự khác biệt giữa điều kiện có thật và không có thật ở động từ. **Nếu tôi là bạn** dùng **là** như mọi câu khác. Tiếng Anh dùng **were** (không phải **was**) sau **if** hoặc **wish** khi tình huống là tưởng tượng, giả định, hoặc trái với thực tế — cho MỌI chủ ngữ, kể cả **I**, **he**, và **she**.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia tidak menandai perbedaan antara kondisi nyata dan tidak nyata pada bentuk kata kerja. **Kalau saya jadi kamu** menggunakan kata kerja yang sama seperti kalimat biasa. Bahasa Inggris menggunakan **were** (bukan **was**) setelah **if** atau **wish** saat situasinya imajiner, hipotetis, atau bertentangan dengan fakta — untuk SEMUA subjek, bahkan **I**, **he**, dan **she**.

pattern.en: Use **were** (not **was**) in two places: (1) After **if** in unreal present/future conditions: **If I were you**, **If she were here**, **If it were possible**. (2) After **wish** for present unreal situations: **I wish I were taller**, **He wishes he were at the beach**. The key test: if the situation is NOT true right now, use **were**.
pattern.vi: Dùng **were** (không phải **was**) ở hai chỗ: (1) Sau **if** trong điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại/tương lai: **If I were you**, **If she were here**, **If it were possible**. (2) Sau **wish** cho tình huống không có thật ở hiện tại: **I wish I were taller**, **He wishes he were at the beach**. Cách kiểm tra: nếu tình huống KHÔNG có thật ngay lúc này, dùng **were**.
pattern.id: Gunakan **were** (bukan **was**) di dua tempat: (1) Setelah **if** dalam kondisi tidak nyata saat ini/masa depan: **If I were you**, **If she were here**, **If it were possible**. (2) Setelah **wish** untuk situasi tidak nyata saat ini: **I wish I were taller**, **He wishes he were at the beach**. Tes kuncinya: jika situasinya TIDAK benar saat ini, gunakan **were**.

practice.en: Say each one out loud and notice how **were** sounds more formal and controlled than **was**: "If I were you, I would accept." "If she were here, she would agree." "I wish I were better at maths." "He wishes he were on holiday right now." "If it were easier, everyone would do it."
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng và để ý **were** nghe trang trọng và kiểm soát hơn **was**: "If I were you, I would accept." "If she were here, she would agree." "I wish I were better at maths." "He wishes he were on holiday right now." "If it were easier, everyone would do it."
practice.id: Ucapkan setiap kalimat dengan keras dan perhatikan bagaimana **were** terdengar lebih formal dan terkendali daripada **was**: "If I were you, I would accept." "If she were here, she would agree." "I wish I were better at maths." "He wishes he were on holiday right now." "If it were easier, everyone would do it."

takeaway.en: Unreal situation → **were** for every subject. **If I were**, **if she were**, **I wish I were** — always.
takeaway.vi: Tình huống không có thật → **were** cho mọi chủ ngữ. **If I were**, **if she were**, **I wish I were** — luôn luôn.
takeaway.id: Situasi tidak nyata → **were** untuk setiap subjek. **If I were**, **if she were**, **I wish I were** — selalu.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: If I was you, I would take the job.
If I were you, I would take the job.
If I am you, I would take the job.
If I be you, I would take the job.
quiz.correctAnswer: If I were you, I would take the job.

explanation.en: Unreal condition → **were** for every subject, including **I**.
explanation.vi: Điều kiện không có thật → **were** cho mọi chủ ngữ, kể cả **I**.
explanation.id: Kondisi tidak nyata → **were** untuk setiap subjek, termasuk **I**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: I wish I ___ taller.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: I wish I ___ taller.

explanation.en: After **wish** for an unreal present situation, use **were** — even for **I**.
explanation.vi: Sau **wish** cho tình huống không có thật ở hiện tại, dùng **were** — kể cả cho **I**.
explanation.id: Setelah **wish** untuk situasi tidak nyata saat ini, gunakan **were** — bahkan untuk **I**.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: If she was here, she would help us.
If she were here, she would help us.
If she is here, she would help us.
If she be here, she would help us.
quiz.correctAnswer: If she were here, she would help us.

explanation.en: **She is not here** → unreal → **if she were**, not **if she was**.
explanation.vi: **Cô ấy không có ở đây** → không có thật → **if she were**, không phải **if she was**.
explanation.id: **Dia tidak di sini** → tidak nyata → **if she were**, bukan **if she was**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: He wishes he ___ on holiday right now.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: He wishes he ___ on holiday right now.

explanation.en: **wish** + unreal present → **were** for all subjects, including **he**.
explanation.vi: **wish** + không có thật ở hiện tại → **were** cho mọi chủ ngữ, kể cả **he**.
explanation.id: **wish** + tidak nyata saat ini → **were** untuk semua subjek, termasuk **he**.

question.en: Which sentence is correct in formal English?
question.vi: Câu nào đúng trong tiếng Anh trang trọng?

options: If it was possible, I would fly there.
If it were possible, I would fly there.
If it is possible, I would fly there.
If it be possible, I would fly there.
quiz.correctAnswer: If it were possible, I would fly there.

explanation.en: **It is not possible** → unreal condition → **if it were** is the formal/correct form.
explanation.vi: **Điều đó không khả thi** → điều kiện không có thật → **if it were** là dạng trang trọng/đúng.
explanation.id: **Itu tidak mungkin** → kondisi tidak nyata → **if it were** adalah bentuk formal/benar.

title.en: Negative inversion — flip the subject and auxiliary
title.vi: Đảo ngữ phủ định — đảo chủ ngữ và trợ động từ

hook.en: "Never I have seen such a view." The words are all English, but the order sounds off. That's because English has a special rule: when a negative word opens the sentence, the subject and auxiliary **swap places**.
hook.vi: "Never I have seen such a view." Từ nào cũng là tiếng Anh, nhưng thứ tự nghe sai. Đó là vì tiếng Anh có một quy tắc đặc biệt: khi một từ phủ định mở đầu câu, chủ ngữ và trợ động từ **đổi chỗ** cho nhau.
hook.id: "Never I have seen such a view." Semua katanya bahasa Inggris, tapi urutannya terdengar aneh. Itu karena bahasa Inggris punya aturan khusus: saat kata negatif membuka kalimat, subjek dan auxiliary **bertukar tempat**.

why.en: Vietnamese word order is flexible — **Chưa bao giờ tôi thấy** puts the negative time word first with no structural change to the rest of the sentence. English demands inversion: the negative adverbial pulls the auxiliary to the front, and the subject follows. **Never have I seen** — not **Never I have seen**.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt mình trật tự từ linh hoạt — **Chưa bao giờ tôi thấy** đặt từ phủ định lên đầu mà không thay đổi cấu trúc phần còn lại. Tiếng Anh đòi hỏi đảo ngữ: trạng từ phủ định kéo trợ động từ lên trước, và chủ ngữ theo sau. **Never have I seen** — không phải **Never I have seen**.
why.id: Urutan kata bahasa Indonesia fleksibel — **Belum pernah saya melihat** menempatkan kata negatif di depan tanpa perubahan struktur di sisa kalimat. Bahasa Inggris menuntut inversi: kata keterangan negatif menarik auxiliary ke depan, dan subjek mengikuti. **Never have I seen** — bukan **Never I have seen**.

pattern.en: Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Common triggers: **Never** (*Never have I felt so alive*), **Seldom / Rarely** (*Rarely do we see such dedication*), **Not only** (*Not only did she finish, she won*), **Hardly / Scarcely** (*Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang*), **No sooner** (*No sooner had we left than it started raining*). If there's no auxiliary in the original, add **do / does / did**.
pattern.vi: Trạng từ phủ định + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ + động từ chính. Các từ kích hoạt thường gặp: **Never** (*Never have I felt so alive*), **Seldom / Rarely** (*Rarely do we see such dedication*), **Not only** (*Not only did she finish, she won*), **Hardly / Scarcely** (*Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang*), **No sooner** (*No sooner had we left than it started raining*). Nếu câu gốc không có trợ động từ, thêm **do / does / did**.
pattern.id: Kata keterangan negatif + auxiliary + subjek + kata kerja utama. Pemicu umum: **Never** (*Never have I felt so alive* — Belum pernah saya merasa begitu hidup), **Seldom / Rarely** (*Rarely do we see such dedication* — Jarang kita melihat dedikasi seperti itu), **Not only** (*Not only did she finish, she won* — Tidak hanya dia menyelesaikan, dia menang), **Hardly / Scarcely** (*Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang* — Baru saja saya duduk ketika telepon berdering), **No sooner** (*No sooner had we left than it started raining* — Begitu kami pergi, hujan mulai turun). Jika kalimat asli tidak punya auxiliary, tambahkan **do / does / did**.

practice.en: Try these aloud with the inversion — the rhythm is different from normal English, and that's the point: "Never have I felt so alive." "Rarely do we see such kindness." "Not only did she pass, she got the top score." "Hardly had I arrived when they called my name." "No sooner had we sat down than the show began."
practice.vi: Hãy nói thành tiếng với đảo ngữ — nhịp điệu khác với tiếng Anh thông thường, và đó chính là điểm nhấn: "Never have I felt so alive." "Rarely do we see such kindness." "Not only did she pass, she got the top score." "Hardly had I arrived when they called my name." "No sooner had we sat down than the show began."
practice.id: Coba ucapkan dengan keras dengan inversi — ritmenya berbeda dari bahasa Inggris biasa, dan itulah intinya: "Never have I felt so alive." "Rarely do we see such kindness." "Not only did she pass, she got the top score." "Hardly had I arrived when they called my name." "No sooner had we sat down than the show began."

takeaway.en: Negative word opens the sentence → swap subject and auxiliary. **Never I have** → **Never have I**. Add **do/does/did** if there's no auxiliary to swap.
takeaway.vi: Từ phủ định mở đầu câu → đảo chủ ngữ và trợ động từ. **Never I have** → **Never have I**. Thêm **do/does/did** nếu không có trợ động từ để đảo.
takeaway.id: Kata negatif membuka kalimat → tukar subjek dan auxiliary. **Never I have** → **Never have I**. Tambahkan **do/does/did** jika tidak ada auxiliary untuk ditukar.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Never I have seen such a view.
Never have I seen such a view.
Never I seen such a view.
Never seen I have such a view.
quiz.correctAnswer: Never have I seen such a view.

explanation.en: **Never** opens → auxiliary **have** inverts with subject **I**: **Never have I seen**.
explanation.vi: **Never** mở đầu → trợ động từ **have** đảo với chủ ngữ **I**: **Never have I seen**.
explanation.id: **Never** membuka → auxiliary **have** bertukar dengan subjek **I**: **Never have I seen**.

question.en: Fill in the blank: Rarely ___ such dedication.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Rarely ___ such dedication.

explanation.en: No auxiliary in the original → add **do** and invert: **do we see**.
explanation.vi: Câu gốc không có trợ động từ → thêm **do** và đảo: **do we see**.
explanation.id: Tidak ada auxiliary di kalimat asli → tambahkan **do** dan tukar: **do we see**.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Not only she finished the race, she won it.
Not only did she finish the race, she won it.
Not only she did finish the race, she won it.
Not only finished she the race, she won it.
quiz.correctAnswer: Not only did she finish the race, she won it.

explanation.en: **Not only** triggers inversion → **did she finish** (add **did** + invert).
explanation.vi: **Not only** kích hoạt đảo ngữ → **did she finish** (thêm **did** + đảo).
explanation.id: **Not only** memicu inversi → **did she finish** (tambahkan **did** + tukar).

question.en: Fill in the blank: Hardly ___ down when the phone rang.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Hardly ___ down when the phone rang.

explanation.en: **Hardly** triggers inversion with the existing auxiliary **had**: **had I sat**.
explanation.vi: **Hardly** kích hoạt đảo ngữ với trợ động từ sẵn có **had**: **had I sat**.
explanation.id: **Hardly** memicu inversi dengan auxiliary yang sudah ada **had**: **had I sat**.

question.en: Which sentence is correct?
question.vi: Câu nào đúng?

options: No sooner we had arrived than it started raining.
No sooner had we arrived than it started raining.
No sooner we arrived than it started raining.
No sooner did we had arrived than it started raining.
quiz.correctAnswer: No sooner had we arrived than it started raining.

explanation.en: **No sooner** → invert existing auxiliary **had** with subject **we**: **had we arrived**.
explanation.vi: **No sooner** → đảo trợ động từ **had** với chủ ngữ **we**: **had we arrived**.
explanation.id: **No sooner** → tukar auxiliary **had** dengan subjek **we**: **had we arrived**.

title.en: Inversion — flip the word order for impact
title.vi: Đảo ngữ — đảo trật tự từ để nhấn mạnh
title.id: Inversi — balik urutan kata untuk dampak
title.hi: **Never have I** — ज़ोर देने के लिए inversion

hook.en: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Sounds almost right to an Indonesian ear — **tidak pernah saya lihat** is natural in Indonesian. But English demands the verb flip: **Never have I seen…**
hook.vi: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Nghe gần đúng với tai người Việt — **chưa bao giờ tôi thấy** là tự nhiên trong tiếng Việt. Nhưng tiếng Anh đòi hỏi đảo động từ: **Never have I seen…**
hook.id: "Never I have seen such a beautiful view." Kedengarannya hampir benar di telinga orang Indonesia — **tidak pernah saya lihat** itu wajar dalam bahasa Indonesia. Tapi bahasa Inggris menuntut kata kerjanya dibalik: **Never have I seen…**
hook.hi: "Never I have seen such dedication." हिंदी और English दोनों में यह natural लगता है — adverb को आगे रखो, बाकी वाक्य जस का तस। लेकिन English में negative adverb के बाद subject और auxiliary की अदला-बदली होती है: "Never **have I** seen..."

why.en: Indonesian often fronts adverbs without changing word order — **Mungkin dia sudah pergi** keeps subject-verb intact. English inverts subject and auxiliary after negative or restrictive adverbials like **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. The inversion signals emphasis and formality — it's a C2-level feature that separates proficient from native-like writing.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt thường đưa trạng từ lên đầu câu mà không đảo trật tự từ — **Có lẽ anh ấy đã đi rồi** giữ nguyên chủ ngữ-động từ. Tiếng Anh đảo chủ ngữ và trợ động từ sau các trạng từ phủ định hoặc hạn chế như **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. Đảo ngữ là dấu hiệu nhấn mạnh và trang trọng — đây là kỹ năng cấp C2 phân biệt người thành thạo với người viết như bản ngữ.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia sering meletakkan kata keterangan di depan tanpa mengubah urutan kata — **Mungkin dia sudah pergi** tetap subjek-kata kerja. Bahasa Inggris membalik subjek dan kata bantu setelah kata keterangan negatif atau restriktif seperti **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances**. Inversi menandakan penekanan dan formalitas — ini adalah fitur level C2 yang membedakan penulis mahir dari penulis seperti penutur asli.
why.hi: हिंदी में "मैंने कभी ऐसा नहीं देखा" — adverb आगे आने पर भी शब्द क्रम वही रहता है। English में **never**, **rarely**, **not only**, **hardly**, **no sooner**, **under no circumstances** जैसे negative/restrictive adverbials के बाद inversion (subject-auxiliary swap) अनिवार्य है।

pattern.en: Negative/restrictive adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. The auxiliary matches the tense; if there's no auxiliary in the original, add **do/does/did**.
pattern.vi: Trạng từ phủ định/hạn chế + trợ động từ + chủ ngữ + động từ chính. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. Trợ động từ phải hợp thì; nếu câu gốc không có trợ động từ, thêm **do/does/did**.
pattern.id: Kata keterangan negatif/restriktif + kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja utama. **Never** + **have** + **I** + seen. **Not only** + **did** + **she** + finish. **Rarely** + **does** + **he** + complain. **No sooner** + **had** + **we** + arrived than… **Under no circumstances** + **should** + **you** + open that door. Kata bantu harus sesuai tense; kalau kalimat aslinya tidak punya kata bantu, tambahkan **do/does/did**.
pattern.hi: **Normal:** I have never seen such beauty. → **Inverted:** Never **have I** seen such beauty. **Normal:** She rarely speaks in meetings. → **Inverted:** Rarely **does she** speak in meetings. **Normal:** He not only sings but also dances. → **Inverted:** Not only **does he** sing, but he also dances.

practice.en: Rewrite aloud: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Feel how the inversion puts weight on the first word.
practice.vi: Viết lại thành tiếng: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Cảm nhận cách đảo ngữ đặt trọng lượng vào từ đầu câu.
practice.id: Tulis ulang dengan keras: "I have never seen such dedication." → "Never have I seen such dedication." "She not only finished early, but she also helped others." → "Not only did she finish early, but she also helped others." "You should open that door under no circumstances." → "Under no circumstances should you open that door." Rasakan bagaimana inversi memberi bobot pada kata pertama.
practice.hi: ज़ोर से बोलें और inversion की लय पकड़ें: "Never **have I** felt so alive." "Rarely **do we** see such talent." "Not only **did she** finish early, but she also helped others." "Hardly **had I** sat down when the phone rang." "Under no circumstances **should you** open that door."

takeaway.en: When a negative or restrictive word opens the sentence, flip the auxiliary and subject. It's the rhythm of formal, confident English.
takeaway.vi: Khi một từ phủ định hoặc hạn chế mở đầu câu, hãy đảo trợ động từ và chủ ngữ. Đó là nhịp điệu của tiếng Anh trang trọng và tự tin.
takeaway.id: Saat kata negatif atau restriktif membuka kalimat, balik kata bantu dan subjek. Itulah ritme bahasa Inggris formal yang percaya diri.
takeaway.hi: Negative/restrictive adverb से शुरू होने वाले वाक्य में = auxiliary, subject, main verb का क्रम। "Never have I..." "Rarely does he..." "Not only did she..."

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Never I have been so insulted.
Never have I been so insulted.
quiz.correctAnswer: Never have I been so insulted.

explanation.en: **Never** triggers inversion → auxiliary **have** before subject **I**.
explanation.vi: **Never** kích hoạt đảo ngữ → trợ động từ **have** trước chủ ngữ **I**.
explanation.id: **Never** memicu inversi → kata bantu **have** sebelum subjek **I**.
explanation.hi: "Never" से शुरू → inversion ज़रूरी: "Never have I..." (subject-auxiliary swap)।

question.en: Fill in the blank: Not only ___ the race, but she broke the record.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Not only ___ the race, but she broke the record.

explanation.en: **Not only** requires inversion — add **did** before the subject **she**.
explanation.vi: **Not only** đòi hỏi đảo ngữ — thêm **did** trước chủ ngữ **she**.
explanation.id: **Not only** mengharuskan inversi — tambahkan **did** sebelum subjek **she**.
explanation.hi: "Rarely" आगे → inversion: "Rarely do we..." न कि "Rarely we do..."

question.en: Fill in the blank: Rarely ___ such dedication in one so young.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: Rarely ___ such dedication in one so young.

explanation.en: **Rarely** at the start → **does** + subject + bare verb. Present simple, so use **does**.
explanation.vi: **Rarely** ở đầu câu → **does** + chủ ngữ + động từ gốc. Thì hiện tại đơn nên dùng **does**.
explanation.id: **Rarely** di awal → **does** + subjek + kata kerja dasar. Present simple, jadi pakai **does**.
explanation.hi: "Not only" से शुरू → "Not only did she..." (auxiliary पहले, subject बाद में)।

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: Under no circumstances you should lie.
Under no circumstances should you lie.
Under no circumstances do you lie.
quiz.correctAnswer: Under no circumstances should you lie.

explanation.en: **Under no circumstances** requires inversion — the modal **should** flips with the subject **you**.
explanation.vi: **Under no circumstances** đòi hỏi đảo ngữ — modal **should** đảo với chủ ngữ **you**.
explanation.id: **Under no circumstances** mengharuskan inversi — modal **should** dibalik dengan subjek **you**.
explanation.hi: "No sooner" के बाद inversion + "than": "No sooner had I arrived than..."

question.en: Fill in the blank: No sooner ___ than the rain started.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: No sooner ___ than the rain started.

explanation.en: **No sooner** + past perfect inversion → **had** + subject + past participle. Matches **than**.
explanation.vi: **No sooner** + đảo ngữ quá khứ hoàn thành → **had** + chủ ngữ + V3. Ghép với **than**.
explanation.id: **No sooner** + inversi past perfect → **had** + subjek + past participle. Berpasangan dengan **than**.
explanation.hi: "Under no circumstances" → पूरा auxiliary inversion: "Under no circumstances should you..."

title.en: Cleft sentences — put the focus where it counts
title.vi: Câu chẻ — đặt trọng tâm vào đúng chỗ
title.id: Kalimat cleft — letakkan fokus di tempat yang tepat
title.hi: **It was John who** — cleft sentences से focus control

hook.en: "John broke the window." Fine. But what if you need to clear John's name? "It wasn't John who broke the window." That's a cleft sentence — and it does something Indonesian's **yang** construction can't quite match.
hook.vi: "John broke the window." Ổn. Nhưng nếu bạn cần minh oan cho John thì sao? "It wasn't John who broke the window." Đó là câu chẻ — và nó làm điều mà cấu trúc **chính… là…** trong tiếng Việt không làm được hoàn toàn.
hook.id: "John broke the window." Oke. Tapi gimana kalau kamu perlu membersihkan nama John? "It wasn't John who broke the window." Itu kalimat cleft — dan dia melakukan sesuatu yang konstruksi **yang** dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak bisa sepenuhnya tiru.
hook.hi: हिंदी में "जॉन ने ही खिड़की तोड़ी" — **ही** से focus आता है। English इसके लिए पूरा sentence structure बदलता है: "It was John who broke the window." यह सिर्फ grammar नहीं — यह पाठक का ध्यान नियंत्रित करने का tool है।

why.en: Indonesian uses **yang** to highlight: **Yang memecahkan jendela itu John**. English has a richer system: **It-clefts** (**It was John who broke the window**) pull one element into focus; **Wh-clefts** (**What I need is more time**) package a whole idea as the subject. At C2 level, choosing the right cleft structure lets you control exactly what the reader notices first — and that precision marks advanced, purposeful writing.
why.vi: Tiếng Việt dùng **chính… là…** hoặc **… là người…** để nhấn mạnh: **Chính John là người làm vỡ cửa sổ**. Tiếng Anh có hệ thống phong phú hơn: **It-cleft** (**It was John who broke the window**) kéo một yếu tố vào tiêu điểm; **Wh-cleft** (**What I need is more time**) đóng gói cả một ý thành chủ ngữ. Ở cấp C2, chọn đúng cấu trúc cleft cho phép bạn kiểm soát chính xác điều người đọc chú ý đầu tiên — và sự chính xác đó đánh dấu lối viết nâng cao, có chủ đích.
why.id: Bahasa Indonesia menggunakan **yang** untuk menyoroti: **Yang memecahkan jendela itu John**. Bahasa Inggris punya sistem yang lebih kaya: **It-cleft** (**It was John who broke the window**) menarik satu elemen ke fokus; **Wh-cleft** (**What I need is more time**) mengemas seluruh ide sebagai subjek. Di level C2, memilih struktur cleft yang tepat memungkinkan kamu mengontrol persis apa yang pertama kali pembaca perhatikan — dan presisi itu menandai tulisan mahir yang punya tujuan.
why.hi: हिंदी में **ही** या **जो... वह** ज़ोर देने के लिए इस्तेमाल होता है। English में दो मुख्य cleft structures हैं: **It-cleft** (**It was John who broke the window**) एक तत्व पर focus खींचता है; **Wh-cleft** (**What I need is more time**) पूरे विचार को subject बना देता है।

pattern.en: **It-cleft**: **It + be + focused-element + who/that + rest-of-clause**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (focus = the noise). **Wh-cleft** (pseudo-cleft): **What/Where/Why/How + clause + be + focused-element**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (focus = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + clause + be + focused-element**. **All I want is a chance.**
pattern.vi: **It-cleft**: **It + be + yếu-tố-nhấn + who/that + phần-còn-lại**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (nhấn = the noise). **Wh-cleft**: **What/Where/Why/How + mệnh-đề + be + yếu-tố-nhấn**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (nhấn = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + mệnh-đề + be + yếu-tố-nhấn**. **All I want is a chance.**
pattern.id: **It-cleft**: **It + be + elemen-difokuskan + who/that + sisa-klausa**. **It was the noise that woke me.** (fokus = the noise). **Wh-cleft**: **What/Where/Why/How + klausa + be + elemen-difokuskan**. **What bothers me is the attitude.** (fokus = the attitude). **All-cleft**: **All + klausa + be + elemen-difokuskan**. **All I want is a chance.**
pattern.hi: **It-cleft:** It + be + focused element + who/that clause. "It was **the heat** that bothered me most." "It is **your attitude** that needs to change." **Wh-cleft:** What/Why/How clause + be + focus. "**What** I need is more time." "**Why** she left is still a mystery." "**How** he did it remains unknown."

practice.en: Transform aloud: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Notice how each version directs the spotlight differently.
practice.vi: Biến đổi thành tiếng: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Để ý cách mỗi phiên bản hướng ánh đèn sân khấu khác nhau.
practice.id: Ubah dengan keras: "The disrespect made me angry." → "What made me angry was the disrespect." "I just want a fair chance." → "All I want is a fair chance." "The manager, not the team, decided this." → "It was the manager who decided this, not the team." Perhatikan bagaimana setiap versi mengarahkan sorotan secara berbeda.
practice.hi: ज़ोर से बोलें: "It was the noise that woke me up." "It is your support that keeps me going." "What I really want is a quiet evening at home." "Why he resigned is none of our business." "The thing that matters most is your health." हर बार सोचें — किस तत्व पर focus है?

takeaway.en: Cleft sentences aren't decoration — they control attention. At C2, every word you place is a choice about what the reader feels first.
takeaway.vi: Câu chẻ không phải để trang trí — chúng kiểm soát sự chú ý. Ở cấp C2, mỗi từ bạn đặt là một lựa chọn về điều người đọc cảm nhận đầu tiên.
takeaway.id: Kalimat cleft bukan hiasan — mereka mengontrol perhatian. Di level C2, setiap kata yang kamu tempatkan adalah pilihan tentang apa yang pembaca rasakan pertama kali.
takeaway.hi: किसी एक चीज़ पर focus करना हो → **It was X who/that...**। पूरे idea को subject बनाना हो → **What... is...**। Subtle, powerful, C2-level control.

question.en: Choose the correct cleft sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu chẻ đúng:

options: What I need is more time.
What I need it is more time.
That I need is more time.
quiz.correctAnswer: What I need is more time.

explanation.en: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + clause + **is** + focused element. No extra pronoun **it** needed.
explanation.vi: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + mệnh đề + **is** + yếu tố nhấn mạnh. Không cần thêm đại từ **it**.
explanation.id: **Wh-cleft**: **What** + klausa + **is** + elemen yang difokuskan. Tidak perlu kata ganti tambahan **it**.
explanation.hi: Cleft sentence पर focus होना चाहिए: "It was the manager who..." (manager पर focus)।

question.en: Fill in the blank: It ___ the weather that ruined the trip.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: It ___ the weather that ruined the trip.

explanation.en: **It-cleft** uses **be** agreeing with the focused element. **The weather** is singular → **was**.
explanation.vi: **It-cleft** dùng **be** hòa hợp với yếu tố nhấn. **The weather** số ít → **was**.
explanation.id: **It-cleft** menggunakan **be** yang sesuai dengan elemen fokus. **The weather** tunggal → **was**.
explanation.hi: "What I need is..." — Wh-cleft structure, "is" के बाद focus आता है।

question.en: Fill in the blank: ___ bothers me is his attitude, not his words.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: ___ bothers me is his attitude, not his words.

explanation.en: **Wh-cleft** opens with **What** when the focused element is a thing or idea.
explanation.vi: **Wh-cleft** mở đầu bằng **What** khi yếu tố nhấn mạnh là một vật hoặc ý tưởng.
explanation.id: **Wh-cleft** dibuka dengan **What** saat elemen yang difokuskan adalah benda atau ide.
explanation.hi: It-cleft में unnecessary pronoun नहीं: "It was the weather that ruined..." (extra "it" गलत है)।

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

options: All I want it is a fair chance.
All I want is a fair chance.
All what I want is a fair chance.
All that I want it is a fair chance.
quiz.correctAnswer: All I want is a fair chance.

explanation.en: **All-cleft**: **All** + clause (no **what**) + **be** + element. No extra pronoun.
explanation.vi: **All-cleft**: **All** + mệnh đề (không có **what**) + **be** + yếu tố. Không thêm đại từ thừa.
explanation.id: **All-cleft**: **All** + klausa (tanpa **what**) + **be** + elemen. Tanpa kata ganti tambahan.
explanation.hi: "What she said" पहले से एक clause है, दोबारा "it" की ज़रूरत नहीं।

question.en: Fill in the blank: It wasn't the noise ___ woke me; it was the light.
question.vi: Điền vào chỗ trống: It wasn't the noise ___ woke me; it was the light.

explanation.en: **It-cleft** with a thing → **that** (or **which** in very formal). **Who** is only for people.
explanation.vi: **It-cleft** với đồ vật → **that** (hoặc **which** trong văn rất trang trọng). **Who** chỉ dùng cho người.
explanation.id: **It-cleft** dengan benda → **that** (atau **which** dalam gaya sangat formal). **Who** hanya untuk orang.
explanation.hi: "Why he left" Wh-cleft का subject है, "is" singular verb लेता है।

title.en: **a/an/the** — why you need them in English
title.vi: **a/an/the** — tại sao bạn cần mạo từ trong tiếng Anh
title.hi: **a/an/the** — English में articles क्यों ज़रूरी हैं

hook.en: "She is doctor and works in hospital." If you speak Hindi, this sentence feels complete — Hindi doesn't have words for "a" or "the," and your brain simply doesn't expect them. But to an English speaker, something is visibly missing. Articles aren't decoration — they're grammar.
hook.vi: "She is doctor and works in hospital." Nếu bạn nói tiếng Hindi, câu này nghe có vẻ đầy đủ — tiếng Hindi không có từ cho "a" hay "the," và não bạn đơn giản không mong đợi chúng. Nhưng với người nói tiếng Anh, rõ ràng có thứ gì đó bị thiếu. Mạo từ không phải là trang trí — chúng là ngữ pháp.
hook.hi: "She is doctor and works in hospital." अगर आपकी मातृभाषा हिंदी है, तो यह वाक्य आपको पूरा लगता है — हिंदी में "a" या "the" जैसे शब्द होते ही नहीं, और आपका दिमाग़ इनकी उम्मीद नहीं करता। लेकिन English speaker को साफ़ महसूस होता है कि कुछ गायब है। Articles सिर्फ़ सजावट नहीं — ये grammar का हिस्सा हैं।

why.en: Hindi grammar has no article category at all. **एक लड़की** (ek ladki) is complete without any article — the number **ek** (one) optionally adds specificity, but there's no grammatical requirement. English requires **a/an** before every singular countable noun when it's not specific, and **the** when it is specific or unique. Your Hindi-speaking brain doesn't have a "slot" for this — you have to build it consciously.
why.vi: Ngữ pháp tiếng Hindi hoàn toàn không có phạm trù mạo từ. **एक लड़की** (ek ladki) là câu hoàn chỉnh không cần mạo từ — số từ **ek** (một) tùy chọn thêm tính cụ thể, nhưng không có yêu cầu ngữ pháp nào. Tiếng Anh yêu cầu **a/an** trước mọi danh từ đếm được số ít khi nó không cụ thể, và **the** khi nó cụ thể hoặc duy nhất. Não nói tiếng Hindi của bạn không có "khe" cho việc này — bạn phải xây dựng nó một cách có ý thức.
why.hi: हिंदी व्याकरण में article जैसी कोई श्रेणी है ही नहीं। **एक लड़की** बिना किसी article के पूरा वाक्य है — **एक** (one) जोड़ना optional है, व्याकरणिक मजबूरी नहीं। English में हर singular countable noun से पहले **a/an** (अनिश्चित) या **the** (निश्चित) लगाना ज़रूरी है। आपके हिंदी-भाषी दिमाग़ में इसके लिए कोई "खाँचा" नहीं है — इसे जानबूझकर बनाना पड़ेगा।

pattern.en: **a/an** = any one, not specific, first mention. "I saw **a** dog." (any dog, first time mentioning it). Use **an** before vowel sounds: **an** apple, **an** hour. **the** = specific one, already known, unique. "I saw a dog. **The** dog was brown." (now we know which dog). Also **the** for unique things: **the** sun, **the** internet, **the** government. **No article** for: plural general (Dogs are loyal), uncountable general (Water is wet), proper names (India, Monday).
pattern.vi: **a/an** = bất kỳ cái nào, không cụ thể, lần đầu nhắc đến. "I saw **a** dog." (con chó nào đó, lần đầu). Dùng **an** trước nguyên âm: **an** apple, **an** hour. **the** = cái cụ thể, đã biết, duy nhất. "I saw a dog. **The** dog was brown." (giờ ta biết con chó nào). **the** cho thứ duy nhất: **the** sun, **the** internet. **Không mạo từ** cho: số nhiều chung chung (Dogs are loyal), không đếm được chung chung (Water is wet), tên riêng (India, Monday).
pattern.hi: **a/an** = कोई भी एक, अनिश्चित, पहली बार ज़िक्र। "I saw **a** dog." (कोई भी कुत्ता, पहली बार बताया)। स्वर ध्वनि से पहले **an**: **an** apple, **an** hour। **the** = वही खास वाला, पहले से पता, अद्वितीय। "I saw a dog. **The** dog was brown." (अब पता है कौन सा कुत्ता)। अद्वितीय चीज़ों के लिए **the**: **the** sun, **the** internet, **the** government। **बिना article**: सामान्य बहुवचन (Dogs are loyal), सामान्य uncountable (Water is wet), व्यक्तिवाचक नाम (India, Monday)।

practice.en: Read these aloud, noticing where articles appear — and where they don't: "I bought **a** phone. **The** phone is blue." "She is **a** teacher at **the** school near my house." "**The** moon is bright tonight." "I need **an** umbrella. Do you have one?" "He lives in Delhi. **The** Delhi metro is very convenient." "Dogs are more loyal than cats." (no article — general plural).
practice.vi: Đọc thành tiếng, để ý chỗ có mạo từ — và chỗ không có: "I bought **a** phone. **The** phone is blue." "She is **a** teacher at **the** school near my house." "**The** moon is bright tonight." "I need **an** umbrella. Do you have one?" "He lives in Delhi. **The** Delhi metro is very convenient." "Dogs are more loyal than cats." (không mạo từ — số nhiều chung chung).
practice.hi: ज़ोर से पढ़ें और ध्यान दें कि article कहाँ है — और कहाँ नहीं: "I bought **a** phone. **The** phone is blue." "She is **a** teacher at **the** school near my house." "**The** moon is bright tonight." "I need **an** umbrella. Do you have one?" "He lives in Delhi. **The** Delhi metro is very convenient." "Dogs are more loyal than cats." (कोई article नहीं — सामान्य बहुवचन)।

takeaway.en: Every singular countable noun needs a/an or the. Ask: is it specific / already known? → **the**. First mention / any one? → **a/an**. General plural or uncountable? → nothing.
takeaway.vi: Mọi danh từ đếm được số ít cần a/an hoặc the. Hỏi: có cụ thể / đã biết chưa? → **the**. Lần đầu / bất kỳ cái nào? → **a/an**. Số nhiều chung chung hoặc không đếm được? → không mạo từ.
takeaway.hi: हर singular countable noun को a/an या the चाहिए। पूछें: क्या यह specific / पहले से ज्ञात है? → **the**। पहली बार / कोई भी एक? → **a/an**। सामान्य बहुवचन या uncountable? → कुछ नहीं।

explanation.hi: "Honesty" एक abstract/uncountable noun है, सामान्य अर्थ में → कोई article नहीं। लेकिन "the best" (superlative) के साथ **the** ज़रूरी है।

title.en: Prepositions — where to put them in English
title.vi: Giới từ — đặt chúng ở đâu trong tiếng Anh
title.hi: Prepositions — English में इन्हें कहाँ रखें

hook.en: "I am going market to." If this looks right to you, your Hindi brain is in charge. Hindi puts relationship words AFTER the noun — **बाज़ार को** (bazaar ko, 'market to'). English puts them BEFORE — **to the market**. The whole word order flips, and if you don't catch it, your English keeps a Hindi skeleton.
hook.vi: "I am going market to." Nếu câu này trông đúng với bạn, não tiếng Hindi của bạn đang điều khiển. Tiếng Hindi đặt từ quan hệ SAU danh từ — **बाज़ार को** (bazaar ko, 'chợ đến'). Tiếng Anh đặt chúng TRƯỚC — **to the market**. Toàn bộ trật tự từ đảo ngược, và nếu bạn không để ý, tiếng Anh của bạn vẫn giữ khung xương tiếng Hindi.
hook.hi: "I am going market to." अगर यह वाक्य आपको सही लगता है, तो आपका हिंदी दिमाग़ काबू में है। हिंदी में संबंध सूचक शब्द संज्ञा के बाद आते हैं — **बाज़ार को** (bazaar ko)। English में ये पहले आते हैं — **to the market**। पूरा शब्द क्रम उल्टा है, और अगर आपने ध्यान न दिया, तो आपकी English में हिंदी का ढाँचा बना रहेगा।

why.en: Hindi uses **postpositions** — words like **में** (mein, 'in'), **पर** (par, 'on'), **से** (se, 'from'), **को** (ko, 'to') that attach AFTER the noun: **मेज़ पर** (mez par = table on). English uses **prepositions** before the noun: **on the table**. Your L1 word order is the exact reverse. This is especially tricky in long sentences where the preposition gets separated from its noun: "Which city do you come **from**?" (preposition stranded at the end — natural in English, but your Hindi brain wants to put it right after the noun).
why.vi: Tiếng Hindi dùng **hậu từ** — các từ như **में** (mein, 'trong'), **पर** (par, 'trên'), **से** (se, 'từ'), **को** (ko, 'đến') gắn SAU danh từ: **मेज़ पर** (mez par = bàn trên). Tiếng Anh dùng **giới từ** trước danh từ: **on the table**. Trật tự từ L1 của bạn là đảo ngược chính xác. Điều này đặc biệt khó trong câu dài khi giới từ bị tách khỏi danh từ: "Which city do you come **from**?" (giới từ cuối câu — tự nhiên trong tiếng Anh, nhưng não tiếng Hindi muốn đặt nó ngay sau danh từ).
why.hi: हिंदी में **postpositions** का इस्तेमाल होता है — **में**, **पर**, **से**, **को** जैसे शब्द जो संज्ञा के बाद आते हैं: **मेज़ पर** (mez par = table on)। English में **prepositions** संज्ञा से पहले आते हैं: **on the table**। आपकी मातृभाषा का शब्द क्रम इसका ठीक उल्टा है। यह खासकर लंबे वाक्यों में मुश्किल हो जाता है जहाँ preposition अपने noun से अलग हो जाता है: "Which city do you come **from**?" (preposition आखिर में — English में natural, पर आपका हिंदी दिमाग़ इसे noun के फ़ौरन बाद रखना चाहता है)।

pattern.en: **Place:** on the table, in the room, at the door, under the chair, near the station. **Direction:** to the market, from Delhi, towards the bridge. **Time:** at 5pm, on Monday, in July, since morning, for two hours. **Phrasal verbs:** turn **on**, give **up**, look **after** (these are verbs with built-in prepositions — learn them as one unit). **Stranded prepositions:** "Who are you talking **to**?" "What are you looking **at**?" (preposition at end = natural English).
pattern.vi: **Nơi chốn:** on the table, in the room, at the door, under the chair, near the station. **Hướng:** to the market, from Delhi, towards the bridge. **Thời gian:** at 5pm, on Monday, in July, since morning, for two hours. **Cụm động từ:** turn **on**, give **up**, look **after** (động từ có giới từ gắn liền — học như một đơn vị). **Giới từ cuối câu:** "Who are you talking **to**?" "What are you looking **at**?" (giới từ cuối câu = tiếng Anh tự nhiên).
pattern.hi: **स्थान:** on the table, in the room, at the door, under the chair, near the station। **दिशा:** to the market, from Delhi, towards the bridge। **समय:** at 5pm, on Monday, in July, since morning, for two hours। **Phrasal verbs:** turn **on**, give **up**, look **after** (ये verb के साथ जुड़े prepositions हैं — एक इकाई के रूप में सीखें)। **अंत में preposition:** "Who are you talking **to**?" "What are you looking **at**?" (अंत में preposition = natural English)।

practice.en: Read aloud, feeling the English order: "Put the book **on the table**." (not: table on). "She walked **to the station**." (not: station to). "I'm coming **from Mumbai**." (not: Mumbai from). "Who are you waiting **for**?" (preposition at end — feels wrong to you, sounds right to English ears). "This is the house I grew up **in**." "What did you want to talk **about**?"
practice.vi: Đọc thành tiếng, cảm nhận trật tự tiếng Anh: "Put the book **on the table**." (không phải: table on). "She walked **to the station**." (không phải: station to). "I'm coming **from Mumbai**." (không phải: Mumbai from). "Who are you waiting **for**?" (giới từ cuối câu — bạn thấy sai, nhưng tai Anh thấy đúng). "This is the house I grew up **in**." "What did you want to talk **about**?"
practice.hi: ज़ोर से पढ़ें और English क्रम महसूस करें: "Put the book **on the table**." (table on नहीं)। "She walked **to the station**." (station to नहीं)। "I'm coming **from Mumbai**." (Mumbai from नहीं)। "Who are you waiting **for**?" (preposition आखिर में — आपको गलत लगे, English कानों को सही)। "This is the house I grew up **in**." "What did you want to talk **about**?"

takeaway.en: English preposition always comes before its noun. If it's stranded at the end, that's a question or relative clause — learn to trust that pattern.
takeaway.vi: Giới từ tiếng Anh luôn đứng trước danh từ của nó. Nếu nó ở cuối câu, đó là câu hỏi hoặc mệnh đề quan hệ — hãy học cách tin tưởng mẫu đó.
takeaway.hi: English preposition हमेशा अपने noun से पहले आता है। अगर वह अंत में है, तो वह question या relative clause है — इस pattern पर भरोसा करना सीखें।

explanation.hi: Relative clause में preposition अक्सर अंत में रहता है: **the house I grew up in**। Formal विकल्प: "the house in which I grew up."

title.en: English word order — subject, verb, then object
title.vi: Trật tự từ tiếng Anh — chủ ngữ, động từ, rồi tân ngữ
title.hi: English शब्द क्रम — subject, verb, फिर object

hook.en: "She her homework is doing." If you've ever written a sentence like this, you're translating Hindi word order directly into English words. Hindi is SOV — Subject-Object-Verb (**वह अपना होमवर्क कर रही है** = she her homework doing is). English is SVO — Subject-Verb-Object. The verb belongs in the middle, and until your brain accepts this, your English will carry a Hindi accent in its bones.
hook.vi: "She her homework is doing." Nếu bạn từng viết câu như thế này, bạn đang dịch trực tiếp trật tự từ tiếng Hindi sang từ tiếng Anh. Tiếng Hindi là SOV — Chủ ngữ-Tân ngữ-Động từ (**वह अपना होमवर्क कर रही है** = cô ấy bài tập đang làm). Tiếng Anh là SVO — Chủ ngữ-Động từ-Tân ngữ. Động từ phải ở giữa, và cho đến khi não bạn chấp nhận điều này, tiếng Anh của bạn sẽ mang "giọng" Hindi trong cấu trúc.
hook.hi: "She her homework is doing." अगर आपने कभी ऐसा वाक्य लिखा है, तो आप हिंदी के शब्द क्रम का सीधा अंग्रेज़ी में अनुवाद कर रहे हैं। हिंदी SOV है — Subject-Object-Verb (**वह अपना होमवर्क कर रही है** = she her homework doing is)। English SVO है — Subject-Verb-Object। Verb बीच में आता है, और जब तक आपका दिमाग़ इसे स्वीकार नहीं करता, आपकी English की हड्डियों में हिंदी का ढाँचा रहेगा।

why.en: Hindi, like most South Asian languages, is **SOV** (Subject-Object-Verb). The verb goes at the end. English is **SVO** (Subject-Verb-Object). The verb goes right after the subject. This is the deepest structural difference between the two languages, and it affects EVERY sentence. Questions, negatives, embedded clauses — they all build on this SVO foundation. When you're tired or speaking fast, your brain defaults to the SOV pattern it learned first.
why.vi: Tiếng Hindi, như hầu hết các ngôn ngữ Nam Á, là **SOV** (Chủ ngữ-Tân ngữ-Động từ). Động từ đứng cuối. Tiếng Anh là **SVO** (Chủ ngữ-Động từ-Tân ngữ). Động từ đứng ngay sau chủ ngữ. Đây là khác biệt cấu trúc sâu nhất giữa hai ngôn ngữ, và nó ảnh hưởng đến MỌI câu. Câu hỏi, câu phủ định, mệnh đề nhúng — tất cả đều xây trên nền SVO này. Khi bạn mệt hoặc nói nhanh, não bạn mặc định quay về mẫu SOV mà nó học đầu tiên.
why.hi: हिंदी, ज़्यादातर दक्षिण एशियाई भाषाओं की तरह, **SOV** (Subject-Object-Verb) है। Verb अंत में आता है। English **SVO** (Subject-Verb-Object) है। Verb, subject के फ़ौरन बाद आता है। यह दोनों भाषाओं के बीच सबसे गहरा संरचनात्मक अंतर है, और यह हर वाक्य को प्रभावित करता है। सवाल, नकारात्मक वाक्य, अंदरूनी clauses — सब इसी SVO नींव पर बनते हैं। जब आप थके हों या तेज़ बोल रहे हों, तो आपका दिमाग़ अपने पहले सीखे SOV pattern पर लौट जाता है।

pattern.en: **Simple sentence:** Subject → Verb → Object. "She reads books." (not: She books reads). **With auxiliary:** Subject → Auxiliary → Verb → Object. "She is reading a book." (not: She a book is reading). **Question:** (Question word) → Auxiliary → Subject → Verb → Object? "What is she reading?" (not: What she is reading?). **Negative:** Subject → Auxiliary + not → Verb → Object. "She is not reading the book."
pattern.vi: **Câu đơn:** Chủ ngữ → Động từ → Tân ngữ. "She reads books." (không phải: She books reads). **Có trợ động từ:** Chủ ngữ → Trợ động từ → Động từ → Tân ngữ. "She is reading a book." (không phải: She a book is reading). **Câu hỏi:** (Từ hỏi) → Trợ động từ → Chủ ngữ → Động từ → Tân ngữ? "What is she reading?" (không phải: What she is reading?). **Phủ định:** Chủ ngữ → Trợ động từ + not → Động từ → Tân ngữ. "She is not reading the book."
pattern.hi: **सरल वाक्य:** Subject → Verb → Object। "She reads books." (She books reads नहीं)। **सहायक क्रिया के साथ:** Subject → Auxiliary → Verb → Object। "She is reading a book." (She a book is reading नहीं)। **प्रश्न:** (Question word) → Auxiliary → Subject → Verb → Object? "What is she reading?" (What she is reading? नहीं)। **नकारात्मक:** Subject → Auxiliary + not → Verb → Object। "She is not reading the book."

practice.en: Say each aloud, feeling the SVO rhythm: "I like coffee." (S-V-O). "She bought a new dress." (S-V-O). "They are watching a movie." (S-Aux-V-O). "He doesn't understand the question." (S-Aux-not-V-O). "What do you want for dinner?" (Q-Aux-S-V-O). "The man who lives next door has a cat." (S-[relative clause]-V-O — still SVO!).
practice.vi: Nói thành tiếng, cảm nhận nhịp SVO: "I like coffee." (S-V-O). "She bought a new dress." (S-V-O). "They are watching a movie." (S-Aux-V-O). "He doesn't understand the question." (S-Aux-not-V-O). "What do you want for dinner?" (Q-Aux-S-V-O). "The man who lives next door has a cat." (S-[mệnh đề quan hệ]-V-O — vẫn là SVO!).
practice.hi: ज़ोर से बोलें और SVO की लय महसूस करें: "I like coffee." (S-V-O)। "She bought a new dress." (S-V-O)। "They are watching a movie." (S-Aux-V-O)। "He doesn't understand the question." (S-Aux-not-V-O)। "What do you want for dinner?" (Q-Aux-S-V-O)। "The man who lives next door has a cat." (S-[relative clause]-V-O — फिर भी SVO!)।

takeaway.en: English verb goes right after the subject. Always. If your verb is at the end, you're writing Hindi with English words.
takeaway.vi: Động từ tiếng Anh đứng ngay sau chủ ngữ. Luôn luôn. Nếu động từ của bạn ở cuối câu, bạn đang viết tiếng Hindi bằng từ tiếng Anh.
takeaway.hi: English में verb हमेशा subject के ठीक बाद आता है। हमेशा। अगर आपका verb अंत में है, तो आप हिंदी को अंग्रेज़ी शब्दों में लिख रहे हैं।

explanation.en: SVO order: She (S) is doing (V) her homework (O). Verb goes right after auxiliary.
explanation.vi: Trật tự SVO: She (S) is doing (V) her homework (O). Động từ đứng ngay sau trợ động từ.
explanation.hi: SVO क्रम: She (S) is doing (V) her homework (O)। Verb, auxiliary के ठीक बाद।

explanation.vi: SVO đơn giản: I (S) speak (V) Hindi (O). Tiếng Hindi SOV 'मैं हिंदी बोलता हूँ' đặt động từ cuối — đừng mang điều đó sang.
explanation.hi: सरल SVO: I (Subject) speak (Verb) Hindi (Object)। हिंदी SOV 'मैं हिंदी बोलता हूँ' में verb अंत में है — इसे English में मत लाएँ।

question.en: Choose the correct sentence:
question.vi: Chọn câu đúng:

explanation.en: Question: Q-word → Auxiliary → Subject → Verb → Object. **What are you eating?**
explanation.vi: Câu hỏi: Từ hỏi → Trợ động từ → Chủ ngữ → Động từ → Tân ngữ. **What are you eating?**
explanation.hi: प्रश्न: Q-word → Auxiliary → Subject → Verb → Object। **What are you eating?**

explanation.hi: Time expression पहले आ सकता है, पर SVO क्रम बना रहता है: (Yesterday) I (S) watched (V) a movie (O)।
